w the step list, an **Expected outcome** field holds the goal sentence the judge grades against.

**Assertions**

Use **Add as
sertion or action** to add an assertion, a second prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote i
t, and what a miss does:\n\n* **Route** — answers \"which tool should handle it?\" and carries that answer's strictness: *Reach th
e tool* allows extra calls, *Exact route* requires the exact order with no extras. The route is always Required.\n* **Step N** — a
n assertion written as a step (what the CLI and the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is labell
ed by that position: a step-level \"no tool errors\" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript up to th
at point. Editing one rewrites that step; it never becomes a case-level assertion.\n* **This case** — an assertion you added here.
It is graded once, over the finished transcript.\n* **Suite** — a default the suite applies to every case. Read-only here, with a
link to the suite's **Checks by stage** settings.\n\nThe list reads as a checklist with progressive disclosure. An off row shows
only its short name. Once on, clicking the name opens an inline editor showing the full criterion, the **Required / Advisory** rol
e control, and any editable fields (thresholds, match criteria). Multiple editors can stay open at once. An assertion that carries
a number (such as a latency budget) shows it under the name at rest.\n\nA row's **role** says what a miss does: **Required** fail
s the trial, **Advisory** shows the miss without failing it. The control appears when your deployment supports assertion policy; o
therwise the role chip shows read-only with a tooltip explaining why it cannot be changed — for example, when the assertion is inh
erited from the suite, or when the backend does not yet support assertion policy.\n\nBecause a failing required assertion halts th
e run, an assertion written as a step can leave later assertions unrun. The trial column marks those **Skipped**.\n\n", "exit_code
